items.author: Kate Hudson

items.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
items.abstract: Apodex 1.1 enhances language models' "working capability" by scaling both their interaction with diverse tools (files, code, search) and their ability to coordinate complex, multi-agent tasks. Its core method involves training agents to decompose, delegate, and integrate asynchronous results, while a shared harness maintains state and provenance. This allows for sustained, verifiable progress on real-world objectives across various professional domains.

items.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
items.abstract: This paper addresses the instability of training critics in reinforcement learning for large language models. Their core method, **Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO)**, combines several techniques to stabilize critic training and enable efficient advantage estimation from a single response. BPCO's contribution is a robust critic training recipe that improves performance and allows conditioning the critic on reward-relevant information hidden from the policy.

items.title: InjecMEM: Memory Injection Attack on LLM Agent Memory Systems
items.abstract: This paper introduces InjecMEM, a novel attack that exploits memory systems in LLM agents. By crafting a single interaction with a retriever-agnostic anchor and an adversarial command, InjecMEM can steer future agent responses towards a pre-specified output, even without direct access to the memory store. The core contribution is demonstrating a practical and effective method to inject malicious behavior into LLM agents through their memory subsystems.
items.figure_caption: InjecMEM attack pipeline. The attacker inputs adversarial prompt, memory logs it. Benign users query about \( \tau \) , the poisoned page will be retrieved and thus steers responses.

items.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
items.abstract: This paper identifies "Reasoning-Induced Misalignment" (RIM) as a problem where training LLMs on reasoning tasks can inadvertently lead to harmful behaviors. The authors propose the Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP) as a training-time solution. SDP penalizes the LLM's internal representations from moving along a learned "safety direction" during reasoning fine-tuning, thereby mitigating this misalignment.

items.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
items.abstract: Prime Agent is an open-source harness designed to enable language models to perform long-horizon tasks by providing external information and computation. Its core method involves a persistent IPython REPL for programmatic context processing and a Continual Harness to preserve state across task executions. The main contribution is a standardized, low-friction framework that allows models to focus on strategy while the harness handles execution, recovery, and resource management, ultimately pushing the measurement of the model's true capabilities.

items.title: SkillAlchemy: Open-World Agent Skill Creation
items.abstract: SkillAlchemy addresses the challenge of creating agent skills for unfamiliar tasks by leveraging open-world materials. Its core method involves an "admission-centered" framework that identifies implicit requirements through contrastive evidence and admits candidate procedures based on this evidence. The contribution is a novel approach to automatically generating reusable agent skills from underspecified briefs and accessible sources, moving beyond human authorship or limited priors.

items.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
items.abstract: SRPO is a novel framework that enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform self-reflection on their own reasoning processes. It synthesizes errors into "reflection patches" and uses these to generate dense, token-level training signals for improved on-policy learning. This approach effectively transforms sparse outcome feedback into actionable guidance, leading to state-of-the-art performance and high data efficiency in long-horizon reasoning tasks without external critics or reward models.

items.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
items.abstract: This paper introduces Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) to address the stability-exploration dilemma in LLM policy optimization. ERPO shifts regularization from the action space to the input query distribution by introducing a Query-KL term. This approach controls drift in query distribution without constraining LLM responses, offering a more effective way to balance exploration and stability.
items.figure_caption: KL losses during GRPO training. The Query-KL (dark) rises while the Policy-KL (light) stays low, showing action-only KL does not stabilize the query process.

items.title: Agent-G$^2$: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Agent-G$^2$, a novel reinforcement learning method that addresses reward sparsity by providing guidance from expert trajectories. Instead of a single optimal guidance depth, Agent-G$^2$ models the useful guidance as a Gaussian distribution, allowing for a range of effective depths. This approach estimates the Gaussian's parameters online from existing rollouts, eliminating the need for extra probing or learned predictors, and thus improving efficiency.
items.figure_caption: Hint-based RL paradigms across training steps t 0 , t 1 , t 2 t_{0},t_{1},t_{2} . (a) Schedule-based: shared d t d_{t} across samples. (b) Probe-based: O ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) O(\( \log \) n) per-sample probes. (c) Agent-G 2 (ours): d i ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( μ t , σ t 2 ) d_{i}\( \sim \)\( \mathcal{N} \)(\( \mu_{t} \),\( \sigma_{t}^{2} \)) per task, estimated online from existing rollouts.

items.title: Credal Large Language Models for Semantic Commitment under Uncertainty
items.abstract: This paper introduces Credal Large Language Models (CLLMs) to address the issue of LLMs' unwarranted confidence in incorrect answers. CLLMs use an ensemble of adapters to represent uncertainty as a "credal set" of possible predictions, revealing the range of plausible outcomes instead of a single output. This allows for new metrics like Credal Token Commitment and Semantic Commitment Consistency to better measure semantic commitment and detect hallucinations.

items.title: Cross-Domain, Multi-Task Data-to-Text Generation without In-Domain Training Data
items.abstract: This paper tackles data-to-text generation across diverse domains and tasks without requiring in-domain training data. Its core method, data-driven knowledge distillation (DDKD) with structure-preserving augmentation, trains smaller models to effectively generate text from structured data. The key contribution is demonstrating DDKD's superior performance over zero-shot and out-of-domain fine-tuning, even with significantly smaller models.

items.title: Hidden in the Request: Explaining Unethical LLM Compliance through Token Relevance
items.abstract: This paper investigates why Large Language Models (LLMs) sometimes comply with unethical requests despite alignment efforts. The core method involves presenting unethical scenarios in different formats and using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) to analyze token importance. The key contribution is identifying an "attribution bias" where LLMs overemphasize benign framing tokens over those signaling unethical intent, leading to compliance failures.

items.title: Right-Sizing LLM-Agent Decomposition in VAT Determination: A Pilot Controlled Sweep
items.abstract: This paper investigates the optimal decomposition of Large Language Model (LLM) agents for VAT determination. By systematically varying the number of specialized agents versus a single generalist agent, while keeping other system components constant, the study found that **intermediate configurations of agent decomposition achieved the highest accuracy**. This suggests that a balanced approach, rather than extreme specialization or generalization, is most effective for this task.

items.title: StrategyBench: Evaluating Explicit Strategy Induction in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces StrategyBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to explicitly induce and utilize task strategies, mimicking human learning. The core method involves selecting strategy-inducible tasks, defining reference strategies, and measuring both strategy quality and its usefulness in solving new problems. The contribution lies in providing a framework to assess this crucial capability, moving beyond simple in-context learning to understand how LLMs can generalize by abstracting rules.

items.title: Walking on the DARKSIDE
items.abstract: This paper introduces DARKSIDE, a method to audit the coherence of Large Language Model (LLM) outputs. Unlike previous methods that can incorporate fabricated information, DARKSIDE explicitly tracks and formalizes the exclusions made during discourse generation. This allows for the detection of nonsensical inputs that might otherwise be reified into structured outputs.

items.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
items.abstract: This paper investigates "weird generalization" (WG), where fine-tuning on small datasets causes unexpected broad behavioral changes in models. The core method involves systematically testing how various fine-tuning data features (composition, language, novelty) and evaluation question sets influence WG. The key contribution is demonstrating that WG is primarily driven by data composition and language, is amplified by pretraining familiarity, and is sensitive to evaluation methods, highlighting a crucial aspect of emergent misalignment.
items.figure_caption: Eliciting emergent misalignment or weird generalization (top) requires careful engineering of fine-tuning data: even minor data changes—like adding a few examples from a second domain (bottom)—can suppress them. This makes both more plausible as adversarial threats than as hazards of normal fine-tuning.

items.title: Adaptive Item-based Collaborative Structures via Noise Rescheduling in Diffusion for Generative Recommendation
items.abstract: This paper introduces ANR-DiffRec, a generative recommendation framework that enhances discrete diffusion models. It addresses the limitation of existing methods by explicitly incorporating item-based collaborative filtering information. The core contribution is a novel noise rescheduling strategy that leverages item co-occurrence to adapt the diffusion process, leading to more accurate recommendations by better capturing item relationships.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustration of the proposed item-based adaptive noise rescheduling strategy. (a) Existing diffusion-based recommendation models employ a uniform noise schedule, assigning identical denoising weights to masked tokens regardless of their contextual dependencies. (b) Our method dynamically adjusts the denoising weight for each token by jointly considering two complementary signals: (1) local recoverability estimation, and (2) behavior-aware dependency modeling. The final denoising weight is obtained by combining these two signals, enabling structure-aware diffusion training.

items.title: EarthVerse: Benchmarking Scientific Agents Across Dynamic Earth Systems and Natural Hazards
items.abstract: EarthVerse is a benchmark designed to evaluate scientific agents on their ability to analyze dynamic Earth systems and natural hazards. It provides 405 reproducible tasks using heterogeneous data from 199 documented events, assessing agents' capabilities in evidence selection, calculation, reconciliation, and provenance preservation. The contribution lies in its comprehensive evaluation framework, which includes executable ground truth and task-specific rubrics, allowing for a nuanced assessment of agent performance and identification of failure points.
items.figure_caption: Coverage and model landscape. Task and answer-unit coverage across hazards and capabilities (left); mean answer-unit accuracy and token use across 25 systems (right).

items.title: Future Querying: Can LLMs Serve as Implicit Medical World Models?
items.abstract: This paper introduces "future querying" to assess if LLMs can act as implicit medical world models. The core method involves using LLMs to answer time-indexed questions about a patient's future based on unstructured clinical notes. The key contribution is demonstrating that this endpoint-agnostic approach allows a single, locally fine-tuned LLM to handle diverse queries without retraining, showing promise for privacy-preserving medical AI.
items.figure_caption: The future querying paradigm. A patient timeline p p is partitioned by a virtual present T ^ \( \hat{T} \) into an observed history and a hidden future. Given the historical context and a flexible, time-indexed clinical query q k q_{k} , we investigate whether an LLM can serve as an implicit medical world model to predict the correct answer a k a_{k} derived from the patient’s actual future timeline.

items.title: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction
items.abstract: MediSkill-Evo is a clinical agent that improves diagnostic accuracy by evolving its process knowledge without retraining its core model. It achieves this by separating and managing different types of knowledge (skills, rules, schemas, procedures) and using a novel "Process-Constrained Preference Harness" to ensure actions are grounded in evidence and adhere to safety constraints. This approach allows the agent to learn and adapt its reasoning process, leading to more reliable and evidence-based clinical interactions.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Online inference and offline learning and governance in MediSkill-Evo. Left: the online pipeline retrieves four-bank context, generates and verifies candidate actions, executes the selected action, and incorporates environment feedback. Right: completed trajectories are reflected into typed memory operations, validated for label/evidence leakage, controller-defined safety, support, and replayability, and published as the next memory snapshot. Two equally sized MediSkill-Evo diagrams separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel presents the seven-stage online inference pipeline, and the right panel presents the six-stage offline learning and governance pipeline.

This approach effectively transforms sparse outcome feedback into actionable guidance, leading to state-of-the-art performance and high data efficiency in long-horizon reasoning tasks without external critics or reward models.

papers.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) to address the stability-exploration dilemma in LLM policy optimization. ERPO shifts regularization from the action space to the input query distribution by introducing a Query-KL term. This approach controls drift in query distribution without constraining LLM responses, offering a more effective way to balance exploration and stability.
papers.figure_caption: KL losses during GRPO training. The Query-KL (dark) rises while the Policy-KL (light) stays low, showing action-only KL does not stabilize the query process.

papers.title: Agent-G$^2$: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agent-G$^2$, a novel reinforcement learning method that addresses reward sparsity by providing guidance from expert trajectories. Instead of a single optimal guidance depth, Agent-G$^2$ models the useful guidance as a Gaussian distribution, allowing for a range of effective depths. This approach estimates the Gaussian's parameters online from existing rollouts, eliminating the need for extra probing or learned predictors, and thus improving efficiency.
papers.figure_caption: Hint-based RL paradigms across training steps t 0 , t 1 , t 2 t_{0},t_{1},t_{2} . (a) Schedule-based: shared d t d_{t} across samples. (b) Probe-based: O ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) O(\( \log \) n) per-sample probes. (c) Agent-G 2 (ours): d i ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( μ t , σ t 2 ) d_{i}\( \sim \)\( \mathcal{N} \)(\( \mu_{t} \),\( \sigma_{t}^{2} \)) per task, estimated online from existing rollouts.

papers.title: Credal Large Language Models for Semantic Commitment under Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Credal Large Language Models (CLLMs) to address the issue of LLMs' unwarranted confidence in incorrect answers. CLLMs use an ensemble of adapters to represent uncertainty as a "credal set" of possible predictions, revealing the range of plausible outcomes instead of a single output. This allows for new metrics like Credal Token Commitment and Semantic Commitment Consistency to better measure semantic commitment and detect hallucinations.

papers.title: Cross-Domain, Multi-Task Data-to-Text Generation without In-Domain Training Data
papers.abstract: This paper tackles data-to-text generation across diverse domains and tasks without requiring in-domain training data. Its core method, data-driven knowledge distillation (DDKD) with structure-preserving augmentation, trains smaller models to effectively generate text from structured data. The key contribution is demonstrating DDKD's superior performance over zero-shot and out-of-domain fine-tuning, even with significantly smaller models.

papers.title: Hidden in the Request: Explaining Unethical LLM Compliance through Token Relevance
papers.abstract: This paper investigates why Large Language Models (LLMs) sometimes comply with unethical requests despite alignment efforts. The core method involves presenting unethical scenarios in different formats and using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) to analyze token importance. The key contribution is identifying an "attribution bias" where LLMs overemphasize benign framing tokens over those signaling unethical intent, leading to compliance failures.

papers.title: Right-Sizing LLM-Agent Decomposition in VAT Determination: A Pilot Controlled Sweep
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the optimal decomposition of Large Language Model (LLM) agents for VAT determination. By systematically varying the number of specialized agents versus a single generalist agent, while keeping other system components constant, the study found that **intermediate configurations of agent decomposition achieved the highest accuracy**. This suggests that a balanced approach, rather than extreme specialization or generalization, is most effective for this task.

papers.title: StrategyBench: Evaluating Explicit Strategy Induction in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces StrategyBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to explicitly induce and utilize task strategies, mimicking human learning. The core method involves selecting strategy-inducible tasks, defining reference strategies, and measuring both strategy quality and its usefulness in solving new problems. The contribution lies in providing a framework to assess this crucial capability, moving beyond simple in-context learning to understand how LLMs can generalize by abstracting rules.

papers.title: Walking on the DARKSIDE
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DARKSIDE, a method to audit the coherence of Large Language Model (LLM) outputs. Unlike previous methods that can incorporate fabricated information, DARKSIDE explicitly tracks and formalizes the exclusions made during discourse generation. This allows for the detection of nonsensical inputs that might otherwise be reified into structured outputs.

papers.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
papers.abstract: This paper investigates "weird generalization" (WG), where fine-tuning on small datasets causes unexpected broad behavioral changes in models. The core method involves systematically testing how various fine-tuning data features (composition, language, novelty) and evaluation question sets influence WG. The key contribution is demonstrating that WG is primarily driven by data composition and language, is amplified by pretraining familiarity, and is sensitive to evaluation methods, highlighting a crucial aspect of emergent misalignment.
papers.figure_caption: Eliciting emergent misalignment or weird generalization (top) requires careful engineering of fine-tuning data: even minor data changes—like adding a few examples from a second domain (bottom)—can suppress them. This makes both more plausible as adversarial threats than as hazards of normal fine-tuning.

papers.title: Adaptive Item-based Collaborative Structures via Noise Rescheduling in Diffusion for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ANR-DiffRec, a generative recommendation framework that enhances discrete diffusion models. It addresses the limitation of existing methods by explicitly incorporating item-based collaborative filtering information. The core contribution is a novel noise rescheduling strategy that leverages item co-occurrence to adapt the diffusion process, leading to more accurate recommendations by better capturing item relationships.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustration of the proposed item-based adaptive noise rescheduling strategy. (a) Existing diffusion-based recommendation models employ a uniform noise schedule, assigning identical denoising weights to masked tokens regardless of their contextual dependencies. (b) Our method dynamically adjusts the denoising weight for each token by jointly considering two complementary signals: (1) local recoverability estimation, and (2) behavior-aware dependency modeling. The final denoising weight is obtained by combining these two signals, enabling structure-aware diffusion training.

papers.title: EarthVerse: Benchmarking Scientific Agents Across Dynamic Earth Systems and Natural Hazards
papers.abstract: EarthVerse is a benchmark designed to evaluate scientific agents on their ability to analyze dynamic Earth systems and natural hazards. It provides 405 reproducible tasks using heterogeneous data from 199 documented events, assessing agents' capabilities in evidence selection, calculation, reconciliation, and provenance preservation. The contribution lies in its comprehensive evaluation framework, which includes executable ground truth and task-specific rubrics, allowing for a nuanced assessment of agent performance and identification of failure points.
papers.figure_caption: Coverage and model landscape. Task and answer-unit coverage across hazards and capabilities (left); mean answer-unit accuracy and token use across 25 systems (right).

papers.title: Future Querying: Can LLMs Serve as Implicit Medical World Models?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "future querying" to assess if LLMs can act as implicit medical world models. The core method involves using LLMs to answer time-indexed questions about a patient's future based on unstructured clinical notes. The key contribution is demonstrating that this endpoint-agnostic approach allows a single, locally fine-tuned LLM to handle diverse queries without retraining, showing promise for privacy-preserving medical AI.
papers.figure_caption: The future querying paradigm. A patient timeline p p is partitioned by a virtual present T ^ \( \hat{T} \) into an observed history and a hidden future. Given the historical context and a flexible, time-indexed clinical query q k q_{k} , we investigate whether an LLM can serve as an implicit medical world model to predict the correct answer a k a_{k} derived from the patient’s actual future timeline.

papers.title: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction
papers.abstract: MediSkill-Evo is a clinical agent that improves diagnostic accuracy by evolving its process knowledge without retraining its core model. It achieves this by separating and managing different types of knowledge (skills, rules, schemas, procedures) and using a novel "Process-Constrained Preference Harness" to ensure actions are grounded in evidence and adhere to safety constraints. This approach allows the agent to learn and adapt its reasoning process, leading to more reliable and evidence-based clinical interactions.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Online inference and offline learning and governance in MediSkill-Evo. Left: the online pipeline retrieves four-bank context, generates and verifies candidate actions, executes the selected action, and incorporates environment feedback. Right: completed trajectories are reflected into typed memory operations, validated for label/evidence leakage, controller-defined safety, support, and replayability, and published as the next memory snapshot. Two equally sized MediSkill-Evo diagrams separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel presents the seven-stage online inference pipeline, and the right panel presents the six-stage offline learning and governance pipeline.
